claims: Easter is a "moveable feast" tied to the lunar cycle and the spring equinox.
Easter is not a fixed date on the Gregorian calendar.
Easter is celebrated on the first Sunday after the first full moon (the "Paschal Full Moon") on or after the vernal equinox (March 21).
Easter always falls between March 22 and April 25.
The Church fixes the equinox at March 21 even if the astronomical event falls on a slightly different day.
Easter must be on a Sunday.
The Easter date shifts to the next available Sunday after the full moon, as explained by Scot Pilie' on Facebook.
Western Christianity uses the Gregorian calendar.
Eastern Orthodox churches use the Julian calendar.
Eastern Orthodox churches' use of the Julian calendar often results in a different, later Easter date.
The lunar cycle operates on a 29.5-day cycle.
